text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Ex-premier Tiit Vaehi said he was prepared to continue meetings with high Russian officials if specially authorized.
- A former policeman arrested unlawfully will have to be paid 500,000 kroons compensation by the state, a court decided.
- British customs officials discovered in Avonmouth port 200 kg of cocaine on a ship on the way to Tallinn.
- Tallinn Department Store will open tomorrow a branch in Helsinki and intends to expand to other cities in Finland.
- Estonia should speed up harmonisation of its legislation with EU norms, EU commissioner Hans van den Broek said during the first day of his visit to Tallinn.
- Housing reform has been delayed due to inadequate legislation, officials in the southern town of Tartu said.

- MP Arnold Ruutel represented four factions of the Coalition Party and rural union bloc when he protested in parliament against the secrecy around the state inspection's report on the Bank of Estonia.
- Parliament gave permission for Estonian troops to take part in the EstPla-4 in a mission in Bosnia.
- President Lennart Meri met members of the Danish parliament, and expressed gratitude for their country's support.
- Estonia may gain WTO membership already this year foreign ministry deputy chancellor Priit Kolbre said on his return from a meeting in Geneva with the U.S. representatives in WTO.
- Tallinn Pharmaceutical Plant will pay 5.7 million kroons in dividends and plans to continue trade in its main market in Russia, the management said.
